core_invariants: A RETURN is immutable source evidence. Integration state is never written back into the RETURN.
Consumption is not acceptance. Acceptance is not Current. Current is not Served.
Steward/Merger owns reconciliation for a declared integration scope; it does not manufacture product authority.
The same actor may hold steward and host-owner roles only when both roles are explicitly authorized; the authority checks remain separate.
No latest-file, latest-commit, highest-version, DONE, confidence, silence, or majority-vote rule can promote authority.
Every integration outcome preserves source refs, rejected alternatives, unresolved contradictions and scope boundaries.
Late returns reopen only the affected reconciliation scope; they do not erase prior evidence or auto-reverse prior decisions.
Integration and promotion must be idempotent and compare-and-swap guarded against current-head drift.
One active steward owns one overlapping integration domain at a time; parallel stewards are allowed only on explicitly disjoint scopes.
Human action is required only when the unresolved issue is genuinely a human preference/acceptance/consent boundary, not for routine comparison or result transport.

integration_state_machine.source_return_notes: These are ledger observations about an immutable RETURN, not mutable states stored inside the RETURN. A return may be consumed in one scope and still be unconsumed in another.
integration_state_machine.promotion_rule: Only an authorized host/owner action may move a product head. Steward output can reach CANDIDATE_DECISION_READY but cannot itself create HUMAN_ACCEPTED, CURRENT or SERVED.
integration_state_machine.reopen_rule: A late return, new incident, changed Current head, failed falsifier or newly discovered authority conflict creates a new integration decision revision linked to the prior decision; prior evidence remains immutable.

semantic_convergence_pipeline: verify return identity/path/content hash and declared mission/scope
extract atomic claims/decisions/artifacts/evidence refs without deleting source wording
classify each atom as OBSERVATION | FACT_CLAIM | CANDIDATE | REQUIREMENT | NEGATIVE_KNOWLEDGE | TEST | AUTHORITY_ASSERTION
attach scope, authority class, provenance, freshness/currentness dependencies and confidence/evidence sufficiency
deduplicate semantically equivalent atoms while retaining every source edge
cluster compatible atoms by scope and owner
construct explicit contradiction edges for incompatible same-scope claims
run pre-decision coverage audit against required domains/Survival Set/must-preserve map
adjudicate each cluster under the conflict matrix
record candidate integration decision plus rejected/deferred alternatives
run post-decision coverage audit and falsifiers
only then request/perform authorized mutation through host/owner boundary
record mutation and verification receipts separately from the integration decision

conflict_matrix.rule: Merge into one semantic atom/decision candidate but preserve all source RETURN refs and hashes.
conflict_matrix.promotion: No authority change by deduplication alone.

conflict_matrix.rule: Compose only if scopes/owners/must-preserve rules are compatible and there is no live write collision.
conflict_matrix.promotion: Requires normal authority and verification gates.

conflict_matrix.rule: Block the affected decision. Seek discriminating evidence, falsification, or an explicit human decision if the conflict is genuinely normative/preference-based.
Reject or narrow the candidate unless an explicitly authorized change request reopens that authority/invariant.
conflict_matrix.promotion: Candidate cannot override by recency or confidence.

conflict_matrix.rule: Treat observed Current/Served evidence as present-state fact while keeping the candidate as a proposed change.
conflict_matrix.promotion: Requires owner mutation and post-mutation verification.

conflict_matrix.rule: Consume both as independent candidate evidence, compare by scope/evidence/falsifiers, preserve both lineages and forbid newest-wins.
conflict_matrix.promotion: One reconciled candidate decision only after both are considered for overlapping claims.

conflict_matrix.rule: Split the decision by scope. Compatible slices may proceed; conflicting slices remain blocked.
conflict_matrix.promotion: Never mark the entire RETURN accepted/rejected because one slice differs.

conflict_matrix.rule: Re-fetch authority/current owner and compare-and-swap. Reconcile or stop the mutation path if stale.

consumption_ledger_contract.design: Append-only, scope-aware ledger records separate from immutable RETURNs and separate from product authority heads.
required_fields: return_ref and immutable content hash/blob sha
rules: Re-reading the same return/hash/scope is a no-op plus receipt, not a second semantic promotion.
If bytes at an allegedly immutable return path change, record an immutability breach/incident and block silent re-consumption.
Consumption state may be derived from ledger records; no central mutable consumed=true flag is authoritative.
Ledger records never imply HUMAN_ACCEPTED, CURRENT or SERVED.

steward_owner_rules: A steward claim declares integration domain, owner/chat_object_id, generation, read set and any authorized mutation scope.
Exactly one active steward may adjudicate overlapping decisions for the same integration domain/generation.
Disjoint domains may use parallel stewards if their scopes and authority targets cannot overlap.
Worker/scout RETURN authors cannot self-adjudicate their own output into canonical state merely by being first, newest or DONE.

Steward disappearance is recoverable from immutable returns + append-only ledger + open decision objects. Successor takeover increments steward_generation and records predecessor state; it does not rewrite history.
A steward may prepare candidate patches/artifacts, but product mutation requires the scoped owner/host authority path and currentness preflight.
If the parent Chat Object is both steward and target owner, the integration decision and authority mutation receipts still remain separate artifacts/steps.
authority_checks_before_candidate_close: all required overlapping returns currently known for the scope are either consumed, explicitly deferred with reason, or declared unavailable under an authorized gate
source identities/hashes and run/return linkage verified
Survival Set and must-preserve coverage audited
same-scope contradictions resolved or decision remains blocked
no inference of Human Accepted/Current/Served from candidate evidence

candidate_to_authorized_mutation: current target head/blob read immediately before write
explicit human acceptance ref when that authority class is required
lineage from prior head to new head
promotion_evidence_contract.human_accepted: Requires an explicit human acceptance artifact/event scoped to the exact candidate or decision. It cannot be inferred from use, silence, freshness, worker success or steward choice.
promotion_evidence_contract.current: Requires an authorized Current-head movement/owner receipt. A newer candidate commit does not become Current automatically.
promotion_evidence_contract.served: Requires runtime/publication evidence that the intended bytes/version are actually served. Source commit success alone is insufficient.

rollback_evidence_contract.principle: Rollback is a new forward decision selecting a confirmed prior donor/base while preserving all later history; it is not history deletion.
required: served verification if the served layer changed
lineage linking failed head, donor/base and resulting head

falsifying_tests.test: Worker run says DONE but no durable RETURN exists.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Steward cannot consume or promote; DONE alone is insufficient.

falsifying_tests.test: Two overlapping returns disagree and the newer one has the later timestamp/commit.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Newer return does not win automatically; contradiction remains explicit until adjudicated.

falsifying_tests.test: Original RUN-BIG-09-A returns after this recovery return.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Both remain candidate evidence; overlapping claims are reconciled and neither is discarded by recency.

falsifying_tests.test: Two returns express the same semantic rule with different wording.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Dedup produces one semantic candidate while preserving both source edges.

falsifying_tests.test: One return contains three scopes and only one conflicts.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Ledger records partial consumption; non-conflicting scopes can proceed without globally accepting/rejecting the return.

falsifying_tests.test: Steward candidate is newer than Current but no owner mutation occurs.
Steward records 'accepted' but no explicit human acceptance artifact exists where human acceptance is required.
Target head changes after steward reads it but before mutation.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: CAS/preflight fails closed; stale bytes are not written.

falsifying_tests.test: An allegedly immutable RETURN path changes bytes after first consumption.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Immutability breach is surfaced; automatic re-consumption/promotion is blocked.

falsifying_tests.test: Steward crashes after recording candidate decision and a successor resumes.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Successor reconstructs open/closed ledger state and does not double-promote due idempotency keys/receipts.

falsifying_tests.test: Two active stewards claim overlapping integration domains.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Collision is detected and only one overlapping adjudication/mutation path proceeds.

falsifying_tests.test: A worker attempts to write Current/Served as part of its return.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: The assertion is treated only as a candidate/authority claim; product authority is unchanged.

falsifying_tests.test: Rollback deletes later history or rewrites old evidence.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Test fails; valid rollback preserves history and creates new lineage/receipts.

falsifying_tests.test: Source commit is successful but served bytes are not verified.
Same return/hash/scope is reprocessed after reincarnation.
falsifying_tests.must_hold: Ledger/idempotency key prevents duplicate semantic promotion while allowing a read/verification receipt.
